title: Dedicated maintenance window impact: smoothing billing and auto-credit reconciliation
creator: Amelia Chen
description:
Problem: Customers with Dedicated pools experience planned maintenance (node reboots, driver upgrades, host reboots, storage migrations) that temporarily reduces reserved throughput and increases tail latency. Current billing treats the whole hour uniformly which leads to contested outcomes: (a) customers receive no automated compensation for short but material capacity interruptions during their billing window, (b) customers file support tickets asking for credits or invoice adjustments, and (c) platform engineers manually adjudicate edge cases.

Goal: Implement an automated, auditable process that (1) detects maintenance-induced capacity loss for Dedicated pools, (2) smooths and attributes SLA credits or charge adjustments over the affected billing windows, and (3) surfaces transparent customer notifications and support artifacts. This should minimize manual dispute resolution while preserving accounting determinism for invoices and revenue recognition.

Out of scope: general burst accounting redesign, per-token metering changes unrelated to maintenance events, and pricing model changes.

Key constraints: credits must be defensible by ledger data, bounded to reserved throughput commitment, and not require full reprocessing of historical meter events for each maintenance. We must avoid double-crediting when other SLA mechanisms already apply (e.g., guaranteed throughput shortages handled elsewhere).
acceptance_criteria: Detect maintenance events tied to Dedicated pools with start/end timestamps and an estimated impacted capacity percentage
Compute per-tenant SLA credit amounts that are proportional to reserved throughput lost and the time fraction affected within the billing window
Apply credits automatically to next invoice or generate a customer-visible credit memo within 48 hours of event reconciliation
Export reconciliation records to the billing ledger with an immutable event id and audit trail for customer support
Notify affected customers via email and Console notice with a short summary and link to the detailed credit memo
Edge case handling: overlapping maintenance events for same pool should be coalesced; manual override path for disputes exists in support console
Monitoring: dashboards show detected maintenance events, affected throughput, total credits issued per day, and rate of customer disputes
implementation_notes: Data sources: host / node health events from infra orchestrator, dedicated-pool telemetry (per-second reserved throughput utilization), and request metering logs (per-tenant request counts and tokens). Correlate by pool_id and unix timestamps.

Detection heuristic: flag maintenance candidate windows when (a) node_reboot OR driver_restart OR storage_migration event occurs AND aggregate reserved throughput served by pool drops >= 25% for >= 5 minutes. Tunable thresholds to avoid noisy badges.

Credit model: credit_amount = reserved_rate_per_minute * minutes_impacted * adjustment_factor. Adjustment_factor accounts for partial degradation (percent capacity lost) and a smoothing cap to avoid full-hour credits for short blips. Default smoothing cap = 4x minute-level credit spread over the billing hour (configurable).

Accounting: create a maintenance_credit transaction type in ledger with fields flattened into tags (pool_id, event_id, start_ts, end_ts, percent_loss, computed_amount). Transaction must be idempotent keyed by event_id to allow retries.

Conflict resolution: if a tenant already received a burst compensation or had a manual invoice credit for the same window, reconciliation step will mark the maintenance_credit as 'reconciled' and skip or reduce amount. We rely on ledger join by pool_id + billing_window.

Performance: detection pipeline runs off of the event stream (near-real-time) but final credit calculation runs as a batched job every 1 hour to accumulate accurate per-tenant contribution metrics and avoid heavy per-request computation.
Privacy/accounting note: credits apply only to reserved throughput charges (not to overage or non-dedicated usage).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable detection and dry-run reconciliation for 2 small Dedicated pools (internal customers) for 2 weeks; no credits issued, records logged to audit store
Phase 2: enable auto-crediting for customers under a labelling group (opt-in) and send notifications; collect support feedback for 4 weeks
Phase 3: global enable with UI controls for support to view/adjust credits and opt-out toggles per-customer
Backout: ability to toggle credit-issuance feature flag and revoke unapplied credit memos before invoicing
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: maintenance detector -> events per hour, median percent_capacity_loss, minutes_impacted distribution
SLOs: reconciliation job success rate >= 99.5% per day; credit idempotency failures < 0.1%
Alert: > 5 maintenance events causing > 10% credit exposure across all customers in 24h triggers on-call billing-eng pager
Support metric: weekly count of manual credit disputes related to maintenance should drop by 80% after rollout
qa_plan: Unit tests for detection heuristic and credit math including boundary cases (5min threshold, 25% threshold, overlapping windows)
Integration tests that run a simulated maintenance event through stream -> aggregator -> ledger write with idempotency assertions
E2E canary verification: for canary pools verify that dry-run produces expected ledger entries and UI surfaces without creating monetary credits
Load test: run reconciliation job on synthetic dataset representing 10k pools with randomly injected maintenance events to measure latency and cost
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Initial design reviewed with Billing and Infra teams. Agreement on detection inputs and need for idempotent ledger entries. Action: Diego to prototype detector logic.

2026-02-27: Prototype detector (kstream) submitted. Observed noisy jitter from transient node heartbeats; increased minimum duration threshold from 3m to 5m. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1248
2026-03-03: Billing ledger schema extended with maintenance_credit transaction type (migration draft LGTM by finance). Migration ticket filed: ENG-46899
2026-03-08: SRE runbook drafted for maintenance events with auto-credit implications. Support team asked for human-readable reason strings in memos. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-10: Began implementing batched reconciler service; dry-run mode writing to audit_store. Observed 0.4% idempotency mismatches in initial tests; root cause: clock skew between event producer and meter join keys. Action: normalize to server_ts in reconciler.
review_feedback: Finance: require immutable event_id and ledger reason codes for external audits. Ensure credit memos are reversible only via explicit support workflow.
Legal: customer communication template must avoid admitting service-level failure language; use neutral phrasing and link to SLA summary.
SRE: detection must integrate with existing maintenance scheduling system (calendar-based planned maintenance) to suppress expected windows and avoid unnecessary credits.
Support: add a one-click 'escalate to finance' button on credit memo page for high-value customers.
